articles.title: Medieval Guernsey reading habits revealed in hidden manuscripts
articles.summary: Archivists discover 17 manuscript fragments from medieval times were repurposed as book covers.
articles.body:
Seventeen fragments of medieval manuscripts that had been "hidden in plain sight" for centuries have been uncovered in Guernsey.

Offering insight into the island's early literary culture, the fragments suggest late medieval Guernsey was home to keen readers, and reading in French rather than English was preferred.

Also regarded as "striking early examples of recycling", historians found the fragments were repurposed as covers for notebooks and bindings for administrative records, meaning they were unknowingly preserved.

Prof Tamara Atkin, a book historian from the University of Oxford, said the discovery "transforms what we can now say about Guernsey's medieval manuscript culture".

Until now there had been virtually no evidence for libraries, collections of books or literary culture in the island during the medieval period, said the States of Guernsey.

Atkin said the discovery showed "books of several kinds - scholastic, liturgical, and literary - were available on the island" at the time.

The fragments - found in the Island Archives and His Majesty's Greffier's strongroom - were identified by the archive team working alongside Atkin and manuscript expert Dr David Rundle, from the University of Kent.

It began when archival assistant Callum Tostevin-Hall was asked to track down a 16th Century copy of Edward III's 1331 Extente of Guernsey, which detailed the Crown's rights in the island.

During his research, he noticed the shelfmark contained a reference to a vellum cover with Latin text that had been removed from the notebook in a previous round of conservation.

"I checked this cover and was astonished to find that it was clearly a reused bifolium from a medieval manuscript," he said.

"Taken together the fragments give an unprecedented glimpse into Guernsey's medieval past, which is not only very exciting for the Island Archives as an institution, but also for me personally as a medievalist."

The team said many of the fragments were in Latin but six of them were in French, with most being popular works that survive in several copies across England and France.

One comes from a dramatic poem called L'Estoire de Griseldis, a secular play thought to have been written by Philippe de Mézières around 1395.

Versions of the Griselda story were popular across late medieval Europe but the version found in the Guernsey fragment was said by the team to be "exceptionally rare".

Island archivist Vikki Hart said the reuse of the fragments as book covers showed resourcefulness "is nothing new in Guernsey".

"What was once a practical act of reusing old parchment has, centuries later, preserved pieces of the island's history that would otherwise have been lost," she said.

articles.title: Jersey earnings rise by 1.2% after inflation
articles.summary: Statistics Jersey says the increase is "slightly lower" than the long-term annual average.
articles.body:
Average earnings in Jersey did not keep up with the rate of inflation for the year to June, according to new figures.

Statistics Jersey said in June 2026 earnings per full-time equivalent employee was 4.1% higher than in June 2025.

However, once adjusted for inflation - currently at 2.8% for the island , external - Statistics Jersey said earnings rose by 1.2%, representing a real-terms pay cut.

The Index of Average Earnings June 2026 report , external said the overall increase was lower than the preceding five-year annual average of 5.6% per year and "slightly lower" than the long-term annual average of 4.2% per year for 1991 to 2025.

It also highlighted average earnings in real terms increased by 0.9% in the private sector and 2.9% in the public sector over 12 years.

However, it said, over 25 years, average earnings in real terms in the public sector decreased by 3% while they increased by 1.2% in the private sector.

Statistics Jersey said the report was determined from earnings data collected from a large representative survey of employers and all Government of Jersey departments.

It said this was the fourth year in which the survey was compulsory for employers to complete.

Matthew Gill, a statistician for Statistics Jersey, said, when looking back at figures going back to 2001, there had not been much a change in real-term earnings.

He said: "It's not necessarily that people are earning less.

"With inflation going up, it is generally something that people will notice more.

"A lot of the inflation recently has been things like petrol, which people notice when topping up their cars and has an effect on deliveries for food and that type of thing."

Heidi Gibaut, executive director at Law At Work, said a lot of the firm's clients had taken on secondary roles to boost their income.

She said: "When I was younger, I did two roles; but it's not a sustainable way of living.

"It's not how you will get the best out of the colleagues that you currently work with."

Gibaut said she felt it was down to employers to make sure the services and products they offered were being done at the right price to stop inflation from getting worse and "ensure colleagues are paid well".

"But it is a really, really hard balance," she added.

articles.title: Tech Town project equips Barnsley jobseekers with AI skills
articles.summary: New courses in Barnsley will offer training as well as paid work placements.
articles.body:
Barnsley residents will be offered support in using artificial intelligence (AI) to train for future careers under two new government schemes.

AI Career Launchpad will offer flexible training and paid work placements with employers, while Getting Job Ready with AI will support jobseekers, the Cabinet Office said.

The training comes six months after Barnsley was dubbed the UK's first "Tech Town", with firms including Microsoft, Cisco and Adobe pledging to support local people seeking "jobs of the future".

AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said: "AI is going to transform the world of work and our job is to make sure working people benefit from that change."

He added: "That starts with helping people understand how AI can be useful day-to-day - whether that means finding a job, learning new skills or building a career in a growing industry.

"Barnsley is showing what this can look like in practice.

"As our first Tech Town, it is helping us find ways that can create opportunities for local people and support communities across the country."

The AI Career Launchpad, a partnership with Barnsley College worth more than £400,000, will offer residents of all ages a faster, more flexible route into AI jobs.

Learners will get six months of training linked to a Level 4 apprenticeship, plus paid placements to gain experience while they learn.

Barnsley College Principal and CEO David Akeroyd said the scheme opened up careers that had, until now, been "concentrated elsewhere in the country".

Local businesses that sign up will benefit by getting early access to people training in AI, with government-funded placements helping them bring fresh skills into their teams.

Once the programme has been completed, its curriculum will then be freely available for other colleges and training providers elsewhere to use across the country.

From September, jobseekers in Barnsley will also get hands-on support through the Getting Job Ready with AI pilot.

Support would include using AI to search for suitable roles, tailor CVs and cover letters, prepare for interviews and understand how employers are already using digital tools in day-to-day jobs.

People will be referred onto the course through Jobcentre Plus.

The pilot forms part of a wider drive by the Department for Work and Pensions to get more people into work and help them progress once there, including reforming jobcentres into a universal careers service.

Matt O'Neill, Barnsley Council's Executive Director for Place, said the authority hoped the schemes would "make a real difference" to residents' lives.

"Tech Town is about using technology in ways that are inclusive, trusted and rooted in everyday life," he said.

"We want to make sure residents, employers and communities across the borough are ready for the jobs and services of the future."

Alongside the two new schemes, an assessment launching in autumn will look at how local charities, community groups and social enterprises are already using AI, and where further support could make the biggest difference.

Lessons from Barnsley will inform how similar approaches could be used elsewhere as the government works to equip 10 million UK workers with AI skills by 2030.

articles.title: Amazon and Flipkart have new cancellation fees for sellers and why they are unhappy with it
articles.summary: Tech News News: The story has been updated with a statement from Amazon.Online commerce platforms Amazon and Flipkart have restructured cancellation fees ahead of the.
articles.body: The story has been updated with a statement from Amazon.Online commerce platforms Amazon and Flipkart have restructured cancellation fees ahead of the festival season in the country. According to a report by PTI, Amazon India has changed the manner in which it calculates order cancellation fees for sellers using its Easy Ship and Self Ship services. As per the notice on Amazon Indiaâs seller forum, the change is effective from August 17. Similarly, Flipkart has also put in place a three-tier penalty structure for lapses in order fulfilment, effective August 23, 2026. The changes, sellers say, adds to the financial burden on small and medium enterprises already operating on thin margins, the report states.Commenting on the report, an Amazon spokesperson said : âCustomer and seller experience is at the heart of everything we do at Amazon. We expect orders placed by customers to be fulfilled reliably by sellers on our marketplace. To encourage timely and dependable fulfilment, we have revised cancellation fees for Easy Ship and Self-Ship sellers. This fee is conditional and only applies in the rare event of a seller-initiated cancellation, which accounts for less than 1% of orders on Amazon.in. We have appropriate measures in place to ensure sellers are protected when cancellations are due to circumstances beyond their control.âWhat is Amazonâs Easy Ship and Self Ship servicesUnder Self Ship, a seller on Amazon packs and delivers the product themselves, using their own courier or delivery service. No Amazon logistics are involved in self ship.As explained in the PTI report, the cancellation fee was earlier based on category-specific referral charges. But after the new change, it will now be computed as a percentage of the order value.âUnder the revised structure, sellers are charged 10% of the order value for orders below Rs 10,000, 8% for orders between Rs 10,001 and Rs 50,000, 5% for orders between Rs 50,001 and Rs 1,00,000, and 2% for orders above Rs 1,00,000, with an 18% goods and services tax levied in addition,â the report says.The cancellation fee is applicable both when a seller cancels an order for reasons other than a buyer's request, and when an order is automatically cancelled because the seller does not ship and confirm the shipment within 24 hours of the estimated ship date.Amazon to increase closing fees across its Fulfillment CenterAmazon is also increasing the closing fees across its Fulfillment Center, Easy Ship, and Seller Flex channels. According to the PTI report, the change will be effective from September 7, 2026.For those unaware, Amazon charges a closing fee every time a product is sold on its platform. The fee depends on the product's price range and the fulfillment channel used by the seller. The fee will increase by Re 1 for products priced up to Rs 500 and by Rs 3 for products priced above Rs 500. Amazon said the increase is due to rising fuel and logistics costs.What is Flipkartâs three-tier penalty structureFlipkart has introduced a three-tier penalty system for sellers who fail to meet order fulfilment deadlines. The new policy came into effect on August 23, 2026. Under the new structure, sellers will be charged Rs 30 per shipment if an order is not ready for pickup by the committed Dispatch By Date (DBD). As stated in the PTI report, a seller cancellation, or an automatic cancellation after three missed dispatch deadlines, will attract a Rs 60 penalty per shipment. If an order is delayed and later cancelled, the penalty will rise to Rs 90 per shipment.Earlier, missing a DBD deadline could lead to a seller's account being temporarily locked, which could have a bigger impact on their business. New sellers will not be covered by the policy for the first three months of their selling journey. People aware of the development told PTI that the new system aims to encourage better planning by sellers and improve the customer experience.What sellers sayAs cited in the PTI report, some sellers said that cancellations were at times caused by factors outside their control, such as delivery personnel failing to arrive for a scheduled pickup. They also questioned why cancellation fees should apply to the seller in such instances.Another seller said the difference in total fees between sellers using Amazon's fulfilment network and those on Easy Ship could be as high as Rs 45 per unit on comparable orders, which the seller claims, creates an unfair competitive situation.The PTI report quotes Vinod Kumar, Trustee of the Forum for Internet Resellers, Sellers and Traders (FIRST INDIA), who said Indian online sellers recognise the need for timely fulfilment and high customer service standards, but that the recent increase in cancellation, dispatch and other seller penalties by major e-commerce marketplaces, particularly ahead of the festive season, was a matter of concern for MSMEs already facing thin margins and rising costs."Sellers should not become the default financial shock absorbers of the e commerce ecosystem. Marketplaces must ensure transparent attribution of responsibility, reasonable and proportionate penalties, adequate advance notice of fee changes and a simple mechanism to challenge wrongful charges. The objective should be to improve fulfilment while making digital commerce more, not less, viable for small businesses," Kumar added.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Mojtaba Khamenei seen, heard in rare video amid health concerns
articles.summary: Middle East News: A new video of Iranâs Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has surfaced amid growing mystery over his health, appearance and whereabouts.According to Al Ar.
articles.body: A new video of Iranâs Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has surfaced amid growing mystery over his health, appearance and whereabouts.According to Al Arabiya, Iranâs Fars News released archival footage showing Mojtaba Khamenei surrounded by a group of people who offered prayers before beginning their discussions.The footage comes amid repeated claims by US President Donald Trump that Mojtaba is in "bad shape" and was "seriously injured" following the strikes that killed his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Iranâs longest-serving Supreme Leader.This is the second video of Mojtaba Khamenei to emerge in August. The footage, however, is undated.It is also the first video in which his voice can be clearly heard. The video showed Mojtaba presiding religious academic discussion with clerics.The video was first published by Mehr, a semi-official Iranian news agency sponsored by the government and run by the Islamic Development Organisation. Its release appeared aimed at countering growing speculation about Mojtabaâs health and whereabouts.Reports of âextremely criticalâ conditionThe video surfaced after reports in Israeli media claimed that Mojtaba Khamenei was in an "extremely critical condition".Israelâs Channel 14, citing sources inside Iran, and an earlier report by The Jerusalem Post, quoting IranWire and sources close to Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkianâs administration, said concerns about Mojtabaâs health were circulating within Iranâs leadership.Iranian officials have rejected the reports.President Masoud Pezeshkian said Mojtaba Khamenei was "completely healthy", dismissing speculation about his physical condition, according to Iranâs ISNA news agency."Someone who can sit and discuss for seven to eight hours cannot have any health problems," Pezeshkian said, adding that he had held a "very good" meeting with Mojtaba earlier in August.Mojtabaâs low public profileMojtaba Khamenei became Iranâs Supreme Leader after his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, was killed in joint US-Israeli military strikes on February 28.Since taking over, Mojtaba has largely remained out of public view.Unlike previous Iranian leaders, he has not made public appearances and has communicated mainly through written statements.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Ajit Dovalâs China visit: NSA, Chinese VP Han Zheng discuss border peace, bilateral ties
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: National security advisor Ajit Doval on Tuesday met Chinese vice president Han Zheng in Beijing, with the two sides discussing ways to main.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: National security advisor Ajit Doval on Tuesday met Chinese vice president Han Zheng in Beijing, with the two sides discussing ways to maintain peace and tranquillity along the border and further strengthen India-China relations across economic, political and multilateral platforms.The meeting came ahead of the 25th round of special representatives talks on the India-China boundary question between Doval and Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi later on Tuesday.Sharing details of the meeting, the Embassy of India in China said, "On 25 August, NSA and Special Representative on the India-China Boundary Question, Ajit Doval called on Han Zheng, Vice President of the People's Republic of China."The embassy said Doval and Han discussed ways to strengthen peace and tranquillity in the border areas and further improve bilateral ties "across economic, political and multilateral fora", in line with the consensus reached by the leaders of the two countries.Doval arrived in Beijing on Monday for a two-day visit to participate in the Special Representatives talks with Wang Yi, who is also China's Foreign Minister.The talks are expected to focus on the boundary question, along with bilateral, regional and international issues.The Chinese Foreign Ministry has described the Special Representatives mechanism as the "main channel" for negotiations between the two countries on the boundary question and an important platform for communication on issues of mutual interest.The mechanism was established in 2003 to address the India-China boundary dispute, which stretches across roughly 3,488 km.The 24th round of talks was held in August last year, when the two sides held what Beijing described as candid and in-depth discussions and reached several common understandings.The upcoming round assumes significance as India and China seek to stabilise ties following years of tensions along the Line of Actual Control.The discussions come amid efforts by New Delhi and Beijing to gradually improve bilateral relations after the 2020 Galwan Valley clash and the prolonged military stand-off in eastern Ladakh severely strained ties.Doval and Wang had also met in June in New Delhi on the sidelines of the BRICS National Security Advisers' meeting. The Ministry of External Affairs had described those discussions as "constructive and forward-looking".MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal had said, "The two sides reviewed recent developments in bilateral relations and noted progress towards gradual normalisation. NSA underlined that stable, predictable and constructive bilateral relations contribute to building trust and better understanding between the two sides. The discussions were constructive and forward-looking."The latest talks also come amid efforts by the two countries to build on a series of high-level engagements between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping.The leaders had welcomed positive momentum and steady progress in bilateral relations during their meeting on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Tianjin last year, after their previous meeting in Kazan in October 2024.They had reaffirmed that India and China are development partners rather than rivals and that differences should not be allowed to become disputes."A stable relationship and cooperation between India and China and their 2.8 billion peoples on the basis of mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity are necessary for the growth and development of the two countries, as well as for a multipolar world and a multi-polar Asia befitting the trends of the 21st century," the MEA had said after the leaders' meeting.Despite the gradual improvement in ties, differences over the boundary and Arunachal Pradesh remain sensitive issues between New Delhi and Beijing.Both Doval and Wang are designated Special Representatives for the boundary talks mechanism. While the process has not resolved the long-running border dispute, officials on both sides continue to regard it as an important channel for managing tensions and maintaining communication.The talks also come ahead of Xi's expected visit to New Delhi for the BRICS summit on September 12-13, which could provide an opportunity for another meeting between Xi and PM Modi and further discussions on the bilateral relationship.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: US government wants companies to pay more while filing H-1B visas, what the revised fee hike proposal says
articles.summary: Tech News News: The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has unveiled a proposal that would dramatically increase costs for employers who are sponsoring foreign w.
articles.body: The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has unveiled a proposal that would dramatically increase costs for employers who are sponsoring foreign workers under the H-1B visa program. According to the draft rule published for public inspection, companies filing cap-subject H-1B petitions would face a new standalone fee of $103,265 per petition, along with the existing charges. DHS says that the measure is aimed to recovering immigration system costs across multiple agencies.What the revised H-1b visa proposal actually saysAccording to the notice, DHS "proposes to establish a $103,265 fee, payable at the time of filing, for all H-1B cap-subject petitions, including those eligible for the advanced degree exemption, which would be imposed in addition to all other applicable fees or payments." In plain terms, this isn't a replacement for existing H-1B costs â it's a new, standalone charge stacked on top of everything employers already pay to file a petition.The fee would apply to the 65,000 visas issued under the regular annual cap as well as the 20,000 visas reserved for foreign workers holding a qualifying US master's degree or higher. It would not apply to cap-exempt petitions, which cover many roles at universities, nonprofit research organizations, and government research institutions.How DHS landed on $103,265 feeThe figure isn't arbitrary. DHS calculated it by dividing the total costs it wants to recover â $8,777,488,035 â by a projected annual filing volume of 85,000 cap-subject petitions, arriving at $103,264.57, which the agency then rounded to the nearest $5 increment consistent with its past fee-setting practice.The agency argues this approach is justified because H-1B petitioners are, in its words, an applicant pool that is "most willing and able to pay an additional fee" compared with other immigration benefit requestors, given that employers are already required to pay a certified prevailing wage to the workers they sponsor.Separate from â and stackable with â the $100,000 proclamation feeThis proposal is legally distinct from the $100,000 payment imposed last year under Presidential Proclamation 10973, which was struck down in June 2026 by a federal judge in Massachusetts (a ruling now under appeal at the First Circuit). DHS is explicit that the new $103,265 fee relies on different statutory authority â primarily sections 286(j) and (m) of the Immigration and Nationality Act â rather than the president's proclamation power used for the earlier fee.Notably, the rule states that if the proclamation's payment requirement is ever reinstated through the appeals process, employers subject to both would have to pay both amounts â the $100,000 proclamation fee and the new $103,265 rule-based fee â on top of each other. The proclamation itself is due to expire in September unless extended, and DHS notes this new rule is intended to take its place going forward.Impact on employersDHS argues that employers sponsoring Hâ1B workers generally have the resources to absorb the fee, noting median annual wages of $133,000 for Hâ1B employees. However, the government acknowledges the fee may reduce filings, particularly among smaller firms. Public comments on the proposal are open until 30 days after publication in the Federal Register (August 25, 2026).Where the money would goUnlike most past USCIS fee increases, which funded USCIS alone, this proposal spreads the roughly $8.8 billion in projected annual revenue across six federal agencies involved in different parts of the immigration system:* USCIS â 34.2% ($3.0 billion), covering adjudications, staffing increases, and IT modernization* EOIR (the Justice Department's immigration courts) â 33.7% ($2.96 billion), funding roughly 8,400 new positions including immigration judges* DOL â 13.8% ($1.21 billion), covering labor certification and wage-enforcement functions* ICE â 11.9% ($1.05 billion), covering vetting and the Student and Exchange Visitor Program* DOS â 5.5% ($484 million), covering consular vetting and fraud-prevention systems* CBP â 0.9% ($76.2 million), covering biometric entry-exit matchingDHS frames this interagency cost-sharing as consistent with its statutory authority to recover the "full costs" of administering the lawful immigration system â not just the direct cost of processing a single petition, but the broader web of vetting, enforcement, and court functions connected to it.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Chinese CEO of the world's biggest and most popular robot company admits that robots still cannot ...
articles.summary: Tech News News: Chinese robotics company Unitreeâs CEO Wang Xingxing has predicted that humanoid robots may still be years away from reaching their own âChatGPT momen.
articles.body: Chinese robotics company Unitreeâs CEO Wang Xingxing has predicted that humanoid robots may still be years away from reaching their own âChatGPT moment.â The chief executive of the world's largest seller and manufacturer of humanoid robots has made this forecast despite growing interest in the technology. Speaking at the World Robot Conference in Beijing this week, 36-year-old Xingxing said the breakthrough could take â2 to 3 years at the fastest, and 5 or even 10 years at the slowest,â according to a translation of his speech previously reported by CNBC.Wang said robots would reach that point only when they can be placed in an unfamiliar environment or a home and complete about 80% of tasks using voice commands or text alone. His comments suggest that robots still cannot easily adapt to new situations and tasks, a limitation he said is holding back the robotics industry.Unitree CEO says robots still need years to reach ChatGPT momentWang's latest estimate is more cautious than his comments at the same conference last year, when he said the breakthrough moment for robotics would arrive within five years at the latest. His remarks also came shortly after Unitree's stock surged 460% when the company debuted on Shanghai's STAR Market.Founded by Wang about a decade ago, Unitree became more widely known last year after a video showed its humanoid robots performing a coordinated dance with humans during China's Spring Festival Gala broadcast on state television.Less than a month later, Wang was among a small group of executives seated in the front row alongside BYD chairman Wang Chuanfu and Huawei founder Ren Zhengfei at a private enterprise symposium hosted by China's president Xi Jinping in Beijing.âArtificial-intelligence-driven robots are evolving at an incredibly fast pace, surpassing my expectations. Every day brings new surprises,â Wang told China state TV following the meeting, the South China Morning Post reported.Unitree returned to the Spring Festival Gala this year, with its robots performing more advanced movements including backflips and jumps over platforms.Humanoid robots still need retraining for new tasksWang said Unitree's robots remain less efficient than human workers and need retraining for each new task. Their difficulty in adapting to unfamiliar situations remains one of the main challenges for the wider robotics industry, he said.Unitree is working on a self-evolving development loop in which its AI tests a robot's âcontrol codeâ and continuously scores the results with human help. The system is intended to improve the precision of the robots' movements, which Wang said can still go wrong in âthe last few centimetres or millimetres.âGet the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay flags off 250 new buses, including 130 electric buses
articles.summary: CHENNAI: Chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Tuesday inaugurated new bus services operated by the Metropolitan Transport Corporation (MTC) and Tamil Nadu.
articles.body: CHENNAI: Chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Tuesday inaugurated new bus services operated by the Metropolitan Transport Corporation (MTC) and Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporations at the Secretariat.He flagged off 130 low-floor electric buses worth Rs 234.5 crore and 120 other buses worth Rs 55.8 crore for public use.The 130 EV buses are from Switch Mobility, a subsidiary of Ashok Leyland and are part of Tamil Naduâs broader green mobility programme.The CM boarded one of the buses and inspected its amenities.Earlier on Monday, CM Vijay announced the expansion of the fare-free bus travel scheme for women, making services such as deluxe and express buses free for beneficiaries.Making several announcements in the Assembly, Vijay, fulfilling TVK's key electoral assurances, announced three free cooking gas cylinders and also declared that the Parandur greenfield airport project will be shelved.The project had been strongly opposed by farmers who did not wish to part with their farm lands."There will be no riders like income ceiling or number of trips for women to avail fare-free bus travel - Vettri Payanam," Vijay said, making a statement under Rule 110.Women can also travel free of charge on Express, LSS and Deluxe government buses operating in metropolitan and urban areas, as well as on regular fare buses in suburban (Mofussil) and hilly areas.The scheme will be rolled out on October 2, coinciding with Gandhi Jayanthi. Vijay said the move will entail an additional expenditure of Rs 6,000 crore per annum for the state government.On the Annapoorani Super Six scheme, a major welfare promise made by Vijay in the run-up to the April Assembly election, assuring six free LPG cylinders to every eligible family in Tamil Nadu every year to reduce household living expenses, the Chief Minister said three free cooking gas cylinders will initially be provided, with the amount credited directly into the bank accounts of beneficiaries."This will reduce the burden of the people who have been spending extra amount to obtain the cylinders. The government has decided to provide the cost of the cooking gas cylinders. Three free LPG cylinders will be given in the first phase and the price for cylinders will be directly credited into the bank accounts of the beneficiaries," Vijay said, amidst loud thumping of tables by the Treasury.The move will benefit 1,30,16,104 families with an annual income of nearly Rs 2.5 lakh, economically backward families, small and medium farmers, differently abled people and poor families."The preparatory work has commenced and the scheme will be launched this Pongal (mid-January) 2027 festival," Vijay said and added the state government will allocate Rs 4,000 crore per annum for this initiative.(With Agency Inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chennai | Silver Rate in Chennai | Bank Holidays in Chennai | Public Holidays in Chennai | Chennai AQI | Weather in Chennai | Petrol Price in Chennai | Diesel Price in Chennai | CNG Price in Chennai | LPG Price in ChennaiStay updated with the latest Chennai news. articles.title: UK to keep Russia under pressure, set up SCALP missile assembly plant in Ukraine

articles.body: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged to maintain pressure on Russia despite what he described as Moscow's "outrageous threats", during his first official visit to Ukraine as the PM.Burnham met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and chaired his first meeting of the "coalition of the willing", a partnership of 34 countries including Ukraine that was established by the UK and France under his predecessor Keir Starmer.The UK government has agreed to allow defence company MBDA to declassify information on British-made components used in the Scalp missile, the French version of the UK's Storm Shadow cruise missile. The move will enable Ukraine and France to work towards establishing assembly lines in Ukraine and allow Kyiv to produce the long-range weapon domestically.Scalp missiles and their UK-produced Storm Shadow variant have already been supplied to Ukraine by Britain and France and used against military targets inside Russia.Speaking during the visit, Burnham said allies were doing "everything we can" to support Ukraine, including drawing from their own air defence stocks and helping other countries do the same."This is the moment to keep up the pressure on Russia, the moment to squeeze their ability to fund this illegal war," he said, while praising the "strength" of the Ukrainian people."Ukraine has been Europe's protector, not a drain on our security but the front line in keeping Europe safe," Burnham added.The comments came after Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov criticised Britain's decision to share information related to the missile's components. He said the move prevented "even the slightest progress" towards peace and claimed that the Russian military was already collecting information to identify missile production sites for destruction."Britain is involved in this war on the side of the Kyiv regime. Britain methodically and regularly adds fuel to the fire," Peskov told reporters on Monday.Responding to the remarks, Burnham said: "Who started the fire? That's the question, isn't it?"Ukraine has been dependent on American supplies of Patriot air defence systems, but its stockpiles are running low due to the war in Iran, leaving the country vulnerable to Russian attacks.

articles.title: Tipu Sultan cutout video with Pakistan reference sparks row in Karnataka, 23-year-old arrested
articles.summary: CHIKKAMAGALURU: Chikkamagaluru Police arrested a 23-year-old man on Tuesday for allegedly circulating a video featuring a Tipu Sultan cutout with a so.
articles.body: CHIKKAMAGALURU: Chikkamagaluru Police arrested a 23-year-old man on Tuesday for allegedly circulating a video featuring a Tipu Sultan cutout with a song containing references to âPakistanâ and âMujahidâ, prompting heightened security in the district, police said.Superintendent of Police Jitendra Kumar Dayama clarified that the action was not related to the installation of the Tipu Sultan cutout itself.He said a similar cutout had been installed at Tipunagara at the same location, around the same time and with the same dimensions in previous years.According to Dayama, police had earlier told organisers they could continue with arrangements followed over the past five to 10 years, but would not permit any new cutouts or decorations.The issue surfaced around 5pm to 5.30pm when the cutout was used as the backdrop in a video and a song containing a word referring to âPakistanâ and âMujahidâ was added, the SP said.The video was later circulated through multiple social media accounts and came to the policeâs attention, ANI reported.Police registered an FIR under Sections 196 and 299 and traced the account that first circulated the video, following which the 23-year-old local resident of Tipunagara was arrested and is being produced before a magistrate, Dayama said.He allegedly shared the video as his WhatsApp status, sent direct messages to some Instagram accounts and other individuals, and uploaded a reel on his Instagram account, police said.Police are also probing the role of others who may have viewed, shared or recirculated the content."We are still in the process of ascertaining their role. If someone else also with intention did the same, then we will definitely arrest them and produce them," Dayama said.The SP said police were also trying to identify the person who originally created the video. A request has been sent to Meta for the relevant IP address as part of efforts to trace the original account.Dayama said the situation in Chikkamagaluru remained peaceful and police had spoken to community leaders. He said action would be taken against anyone attempting to create disturbances.Police social media monitoring teams at both the district and police station levels were also closely monitoring the situation, he said.More than 300 Home Guards, four Karnataka State Reserve Police (KSRP) platoons and local police personnel have been deployed for security, Dayama said. The forces will continue to monitor the situation during the function and the upcoming procession."Everything is peaceful, everything is calm, and this function will go on," Dayama said.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: Blood Moon partial lunar eclipse: How and when to see it in UK skies
articles.summary: There will be a partial lunar eclipse in the UK on 28 August, and may cause the Moon appear reddish in colour.
articles.body:
Skywatchers across the UK could have the chance to see a stunning partial lunar eclipse later this week as the Sun, Earth, and Moon line up in the night sky.

Lunar eclipses occur when the Moon is full which will take place in the early hours of 28 August. It may cause the full Moon - nicknamed the Sturgeon Moon - to take on an eerie reddish glow.

It comes just weeks after the UK experienced its most dramatic partial solar eclipse in nearly 30 years.

Adding to the spectacle, its position in the sky will be low on the horizon, causing a phenomenon known as the Moon illusion. This makes the Moon appear bigger and more dramatic than usual.

How and when can I see the partial lunar eclipse in the UK?

The eclipse will take place in the early hours of Friday 28 August.

The partial eclipse will begin at 03:33 BST in London, when the Moon enters Earth's darkest shadow.

It will reach its maximum at 05:12 BST, when around 90% of the Moon will be within the umbra.

By this point the Moon will be very low in the south-western sky, causing something known as the Moon illusion .

This is a term for when the Moon appears much larger than it is based on its position in the sky - an effect caused by the way our brains process visual information.

The effect is particularly noticeable during a moonrise or moonset, when the lunar disc is seen alongside familiar objects on the ground.

Exact moonset times will vary across the UK.

In London, it will set and move out of sight at approximately 06:15 BST.

A lunar eclipse happens when the Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon, causing the Moon to temporarily move into the Earth's shadow.

During a partial eclipse, only part of the Moon enters the darkest section of that shadow, known as the umbra.

The Moon is not completely cut off from sunlight, however.

Sunlight passing through the Earth's atmosphere is scattered, with shorter blue wavelengths scattering more easily, while more of the longer wavelength red light reach the Moon.

These wavelengths are then reflected back towards Earth, giving the eclipsed Moon its reddish colour.

What is the weather forecast for the Blood Moon lunar eclipse?

For the best chance of seeing the eclipse, astronomers recommend finding a high location with an unobstructed view towards the south-western horizon.

Clear skies will, of course, be essential.

Viewing conditions are expected to vary considerably across the UK during the early hours of Friday morning.

With low pressure in charge, cloud and heavy showers are likely to affect some parts of the country, while other areas remain clear.

Currently, the best viewing conditions are expected across central and eastern parts of England and Wales. However, even here, the cloud cover could change a lot from one hour to the next and is very hard to forecast accurately.

You can check the latest hour-by-hour forecast where you are online or via the BBC Weather app.

articles.title: No longer safe at the rear? How Chinaâs hypersonic weapons could hunt US support aircraft
articles.summary: International News: China has developed hypersonic glide vehicles that can launch air-to-air missiles, a new capability that could threaten high-value US aircraft such as.
articles.body: China has developed hypersonic glide vehicles that can launch air-to-air missiles, a new capability that could threaten high-value US aircraft such as command-and-control and surveillance planes from thousands of miles away, according to Bloomberg.The development is part of Chinaâs wider effort to expand the use of its huge missile arsenal for different military missions. A person familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that China has also added air-to-air capabilities to some hypersonic cruise missiles and anti-ship capabilities to several other missile types.Hypersonic weapons could target support aircraftUS military aircraft such as aerial tankers, airborne warning-and-control planes and flying command posts are designed to stay away from the main battlefield. But the new Chinese weapons could put even these aircraft at risk.A hypersonic glide vehicle launched by a DF-17 missile could travel about 1,500 miles (2,414 km), a distance just short of the route from China to the US territory of Guam, a major American military base.Chinaâs DF-27 missile has an estimated range of about 5,000 miles, putting Hawaii within its reach.Hypersonic glide vehicles, or HGVs, are warheads that can move and change direction while travelling through the atmosphere. This makes them harder to track and intercept than traditional ballistic missiles.No other country is publicly known to operate a weapon that combines an HGV with air-to-air missiles.A report by the US air forceâs China Aerospace Studies Institute this year said that Chinaâs missile modernisation efforts âincreasingly prioritize the ability to inflict coordinated, systemâlevel damage across an adversaryâs operational architecture.âWeapon has major challengesDespite the threat, using a ballistic missile to attack an aircraft thousands of miles away would not be simple.At maximum range, a ballistic missile could take 20 minutes or more to reach its target. This means the missile would need highly accurate and constantly updated information about the aircraftâs location.The process of collecting information from distant sensors and passing it to the missile creates a long âkill chainâ, which an enemy could potentially disrupt.There is another major risk. A ballistic missile launch could be mistaken for a nuclear attack. This âdiscrimination problemâ could make the weapon especially dangerous during a major conflict, as an opponent might misinterpret the launch and respond with nuclear weapons.China expands missile arsenalChina appears to have sharply increased missile production in recent years. Bloomberg reported in May that Chinese missile production rose at the fastest pace since Xi Jinping became president in 2013, based on its analysis of the sectorâs finances.Chinaâs long-range PL-15 air-to-air missile has already been used in combat. The missile featured during last yearâs brief conflict between India and Pakistan, with Pakistan saying it used the weapons to shoot down several Indian aircraft.The Pentagon estimated that China had at least 3,150 ballistic missiles and 300 ground-launched cruise missiles as of 2024. Those figures represented increases of 147% and 50%, respectively, from 2015, when the US began publicly disclosing such estimates.US also develops longer-range missilesLong-range air-to-air missiles are considered important for any future major conflict.The US has developed the AIM-174B from RTX Corp.âs SM-6 air defence missile. Its exact range is classified, although the ground-launched SM-6 can travel 250 miles or more.On Saturday, the US Navy said it was testing the AIM-424 Malice air-to-air missile made by RTX unit Raytheon Co. The missile has a range of more than 300 miles, according to the Navy.Lockheed Martin Corp.âs AIM-260 is also in production but has not yet entered service. It is expected to have a very long range.In Europe, MBDA Missile Systems Services SASâ Meteor is widely used. The ramjet-powered missile can strike targets more than 100 miles away.

articles.title: Looking to improve your TV's picture quality? These 5 setting changes can help
articles.summary: Tech News News: Many people spend hours watching movies, shows and sports on their TV, but only a few make the most of their screenâs picture quality. The good news i.
articles.body: Many people spend hours watching movies, shows and sports on their TV, but only a few make the most of their screenâs picture quality. The good news is that users do not need expensive equipment or professional calibration to improve their TV picture. A few simple changes to picture mode, brightness, motion settings and sharpness can make movies, shows and sports look more natural and detailed. Here are some of the most important TV settings to change for better picture quality.Start with the right picture modeThe first setting to check is Picture Mode. Most TVs offer options such as Standard, Vivid, Dynamic, Sports, Movie, Cinema and Filmmaker Mode. These modes generally aim for a more accurate and natural-looking image. Filmmaker Mode, where available, also reduces extra picture processing. Vivid and Dynamic modes may look eye-catching, but they can push brightness and colours too far for regular viewing.Turn off motion smoothing for moviesIf movies look unusually smooth, almost like a soap opera or live television, motion smoothing could be the reason. This feature adds extra frames to make movement appear smoother.Motion processing can be useful in some situations, but many viewers prefer to switch it off or lower it when watching films. It might be called MotionFlow or Picture Clarity, depending on the brand of your TV.Carefully adjust brightness and contrastThe brightness and contrast can make a big difference to what you see on screen. Contrast affects highlights and bright areas, while brightness or black level setting affects how much detail is visible in dark scenes.A good approach is to use a familiar movie or show with both dark and bright scenes.Don't increase sharpness too muchMore sharpness does not always mean more detail in the picture quality. Instead, it can add artificial outlines around objects and make the image look unnatural. Hence, it is recommended to lower the sharpness setting. Having said that the best level can vary by TV and personal preference.Check energy-saving and automatic brightnessSome TVs automatically adjust screen brightness depending on the room lighting or energy-saving settings. While these features can help in reducing power consumption, they may also make the picture look dim.If the screen appears inconsistent, checking features such as ambient light sensors, adaptive brightness or energy-saving modes may help. articles.body: Goldman Sachs has cautioned that Americaâs energy sector is facing a âbig troubleâ not only from the power supply constraints but also from the looming labour shortage. According to a report by Fortune, the investment bankâs latest report estimates that the US power and grid value chain will require around 500,000 additional workers by 2030 to meet demand. With roles often requiring three to four years of training, the sector faces a significant skills gap. The report also highlights that the energy apprenticeship pipeline had just 45,000 entrants in 2024, which is far short of the 65,000 professionals needed annually to close the labor supply gap. Rising demand for AI infrastructure, which requires even greater power capacity, could widen the shortage further. Goldman Sachs noted: âPower is a critical bottleneckâbut increasingly, the requisite labor presents a structural constraint of its own.âGoldman Sachs points to humanoid robots and autonomous equipmentGoldman Sachs believes that as the workforce is not able to keep pace, the companies would require humanoids and other autonomous equipements as the potential solution. The firm also believes that the humanoid robot market will witness growth and will reach 1.4 million by 2035 increasing from 20,000 in 2025. This decrease in the human workforce will offer 6,900% increase to the humanoid market. Companies such as Tesla, Amazon, and Caterpillar are already deploying autonomous systems, while China has begun using robots for power grid inspection and maintenance.Goldman Sachs is 'very impressed' with MicrosoftRecently, Microsoft offered Wall Street its clearest signal yet that its massive capital commitments to artificial intelligence are yielding tangible, diversified revenue streams. The performance sparked a historic rally in the software giantâs equity, driving its sharpest single-day gain in nearly 18 years. The catalyst came as Microsoft reported its fastest acceleration in cloud revenue since 2022. The results demonstrated that its core Azure infrastructure and enterprise AI offerings are expanding rapidly among corporate clients, while management simultaneously signaled a moderation in capital expenditure growthâaddressing a key area of investor anxiety over margin compression.In an interview on Bloomberg Television, Goldman Sachs Group managing director and senior equity research analyst Gabriela Borges highlighted the shift in market sentiment. âYouâre seeing more breadcrumbs around Microsoftâs ability to pull varying levers on the monetization side that perhaps were not nearly as obvious as before,â Borges said. Following the quarterly report, Borges reiterated her Buy rating on Microsoft while raising her 12-month price target nearly 5% to $640, implying a potential upside of approximately 64% from Wednesdayâs closing price. During intraday trading in New York on Thursday, Microsoft shares surged 17% to $457 -- positioning the company for its largest single-day percentage gain since October 2008.At the earnings call, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said that the company now counted more than 30 million paid users of Microsoft 365 Copilot, the AI assistant sold as an add-on to the ubiquitous Office software. Thatâs up from roughly 20 million three months earlier.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Nathan Cofnas, scholar who exposed Jason Ardayâs plagiarism, says he had no ill will towards him: âThis was about DEIâ
articles.summary: UK News: Nathan Cofnas, the American researcher who first publicly detailed extensive plagiarism allegations against Cambridge Universityâs youngest Black prof.
articles.body: Nathan Cofnas, the American researcher who first publicly detailed extensive plagiarism allegations against Cambridge Universityâs youngest Black professor, Jason Arday, has said he bore no personal animosity towards the late academic. In his first detailed comments to VRT NWS after Ardayâs death, Cofnas stated that he âhad zero interestâ in Arday as an individual and âno ill will towards himâ. He insisted the controversy was fundamentally about diversity, equality and inclusion (DEI) policies at Cambridge and similar institutions. âI set in motion a series of events that led to a tragic outcome, but this was about diversity policy and Cambridge. Arday played only a supporting role in it,â Cofnas said. He added that he had wanted Arday to remain a professor and âlive his best lifeâ.Nathan Cofnas challenges the story behind Jason Ardayâs rise at CambridgeIn March 2023, Jason Arday was appointed professor of sociology of education at the University of Cambridge, becoming the institutionâs youngest Black professor, and his appointment attracted widespread positive coverage. Central to that coverage was Ardayâs account of overcoming extraordinary challenges in his youth. He said he had been diagnosed with autism, global developmental delay, mutism, deafness and dyscalculia, had remained non-verbal until the age of 11 and had only learned to read and write at 18. He also spoke publicly about surviving epilepsy, testicular cancer and a brain tumour. His story of overcoming these difficulties and rising into academia was widely presented as an example of exceptional resilience. However, subsequent scrutiny by The Guardian found that questions extended beyond the allegations concerning his research. Several claims about his academic career and qualifications could not be substantiated. Ardayâs biography at Jesus College, Cambridge, stated that he had held visiting professorships at Ohio State University and the University of Glasgow, but Ohio State said he had never been employed there, while Glasgow also denied that he had held the claimed visiting professorship. His biography also described him as an honorary professor at Durham University, although the university said he no longer held any role there. Arday had further stated that he completed a masterâs degree in psychodynamic practices at Birkbeck, University of London, and subsequently became a fully qualified counsellor, but Birkbeck told The Guardian that it could not find a record of a student named Jason Arday having studied there.His claim to have authored a book with Palgrave Macmillan was also questioned, with the publisher confirming that it had received a proposal but that the book was never published. These findings became significant because they concerned not merely interpretations of his achievements but specific claims about institutional affiliations, qualifications and publications that could be checked against the records of the organisations named. The scrutiny later expanded to his athletic and charitable claims, including his statements about running 30 marathons in 35 days, completing 600 miles in six days and raising Â£5 million or more for charity. The Guardian reported that some institutional descriptions of the 600-mile challenge were subsequently amended, while Arday clarified that the feat had actually taken place over 12 days because rest days had been included.The plagiarism allegationsIn mid-July 2026, Nathan Cofnas, a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University who describes himself as a âracial realistâ and critic of DEI policies, published a Substack article titled âDEI Fraud and Cover-Up at Cambridgeâ. Using plagiarism-detection software, Cofnas argued that numerous passages in Ardayâs doctoral thesis and later academic work had been taken from other sources with minimal alteration. He presented the case as evidence of deeper problems with how universities prioritise identity in appointments.The Substack post triggered intense coverage, particularly in British newspapers. Cambridge announced an investigation on 5 August 2026 into Ardayâs academic qualifications and honorary appointments. The same day, Arday resigned, stating that the pressure had become too great for his well-being and family, while emphasising that his departure was not an admission of guilt. A week later, on 14 August, Arday was found dead at his home in London at the age of 41. Many on social media and some commentators attributed responsibility for the outcome to Cofnas and the ensuing scrutiny. There is, however, no established evidence in the material provided that Cofnas caused Ardayâs death.Cofnasâs response and suspensionSpeaking to VRT NWS, Cofnas acknowledged that his actions set events in motion that ended tragically. He argued, however, that powerful people must remain open to criticism even when it risks causing personal distress. âYou have to be able to criticise such people, even if there is a risk that they will misunderstand it or feel very bad about it,â he said. Shortly after Ardayâs death, Ghent University suspended Cofnas preventively and opened a preliminary disciplinary investigation, stating that it took his public statements âvery seriouslyâ.Broader controversyCofnas remains a polarising figure. He has previously argued that genetic factors play a non-trivial role in average group differences in intelligence, views that contributed to the end of his association with Emmanuel College, Cambridge, in 2024. Supporters see his work on Arday as a necessary defence of academic standards; critics describe it as racially motivated. In the same VRT interview, Cofnas characterised an earlier on-camera remark about heading a future âDepartment of Eugenics and Race Science at Harvardâ as a joke based on his belief that universities should study race and hereditary influences more openly.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Man City to launch formal bid for Enzo Fernández as deadline nears, testing Chelsea’s £120m resolve
articles.summary: Manchester City are set to send a formal bid to Chelsea for Enzo Fernández before next week's transfer deadline.Fernandez is Manchester City's leading transf...
articles.body:
Manchester City are set to send a formal bid to Chelsea for Enzo Fernández before next week's transfer deadline.

Fernandez is Manchester City's leading transfer target before the closure of the window, with the club preparing to test Chelsea 's resolve with a bid.

Chelsea had agreed with Fernandez that the midfielder could leave if his £120m asking price was met but set a deadline of August 14th for a deal.

City failed to meet that figure before the deadline, but believe a deal can be done in the final days of the window.

Enzo Fernández keen on Etihad move: Man City prepare imminent offer after missing Chelsea's deadline

Fabrizio Romano is reporting that City will submit an offer for the Argentina international imminently. Fernandez is keen on the move to the Etihad, where he would reunite with former Chelsea coach Enzo Maresca.

Maresca wants to add Fernandez to a midfield group that has been depleted by the departures of Bernardo Silva , Rodri , and Tijjani Reijnders , while Nico Gonzalez is nearing a move to Newcastle United .

Fernandez was named among the substitutes for Chelsea's 3-2 win at Fulham on Monday and appeared as a second-half substitute at Craven Cottage.

Chelsea are insistent that the club will only consider his sale now if they receive a huge offer and can improve their squad.

A £120m fee would represent a club-record deal for Manchester City, eclipsing the £116m fee paid to sign Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest earlier this summer. The Cityzens are also finalising the £85.4m arrival of Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille .

articles.title: Michael Jordan’s ‘Last Dance’ 1998 Finals jersey could sell for over $10 million
articles.summary: A jersey worn by the NBA star during one of the most famous seasons of his career could set a new auction record.
articles.body: A jersey worn by Michael Jordan during one of the most famous seasons of his career is going up for auction and could become the most expensive basketball jersey to ever cross the block. The white mesh top emblazoned with Jordan’s iconic number “23” was worn by the star during Game 3 of his legendary 1998 NBA Finals run. It was the end of his time with the Chicago Bulls, known as “The Last Dance,” which was chronicled in a 2020 ESPN and Netflix documentary series of the same name. During the pivotal game against the Utah Jazz, Jordan delivered a crushing performance in front of a home-court crowd that helped shift the series in the Bulls’ favor, with Jordan ultimately leading the team to win its sixth championship in eight seasons. The shirt is the only publicly known white game-winning jersey from the 1998 Finals to become available for sale, making it an extremely rare piece of memorabilia, according to Joopiter, the online auction house hosting the sale. “The significance of this jersey extends well beyond the box score,” said Joopiter on its site, which estimates that the lot will fetch between $10-15 million. “This is the type of object collectors wait a lifetime for — an irreplaceable artifact that transcends basketball to become a piece of global cultural history,” said Caitlin Donovan, the auction platform’s global head of sales in a press release. The “Driven to Greatness” online auction begins September 15 and runs through September 29. If the jersey sells above its low estimate it would become the most expensive basketball jersey ever sold, edging out the previous record set by another Jordan jersey from Game 1 of the same finals. In 2022, a red jersey worn during that matchup where the Bulls lost, sold for $10.1 million, more than double initial estimates, CNN previously reported. In 2021, a jersey also worn by the player during his sophomore season at the University of North Carolina set an auction record at the time when it sold for $1.38 million. The current record for the most expensive sports collectible ever sold is held by Babe Ruth’s “Called Shot” jersey, which sold for $24.12 million in 2024. Ruth wore the jersey during Game 3 of the 1932 World Series, when he appeared to gesture toward something in center field just before hitting a fifth-inning home run into the bleachers, a story which is now part of baseball lore. Still, Jordan remains one of the most celebrated athletes, with online memorabilia sales consistently topping current top stars. E-Bay users have spent more than $88 million on Jordan playing cards this year alone, according to Gemrate, a site that tracks trading card grading and sales dates — beating out every other current and previous NBA player and putting him only below Los Angeles Dodgers’ baseball star Shohei Ohtani.

articles.title: In 1912, New Zealand released wallabies near Rotorua; they now occupy more than 200,000 hectares and, if left unchecked, could spread across a third of the country by 2065, causing $84 million in damage a year
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Wallabies introduced to New Zealand more than a century ago have spread across more than 200,000 hectares in the countryâs North Island. Authorities a.
articles.body: Wallabies introduced to New Zealand more than a century ago have spread across more than 200,000 hectares in the countryâs North Island. Authorities are now working to control their population because the animals can damage native forests, compete with farm animals for pasture and harm young trees in plantations.A wallaby is a small or middle-sized macropod native to Australia and New Guinea The wallabies in the Bay of Plenty region were brought from Australia. According to Bay of Plenty region of New Zealandâs North Island, Dama and parma wallabies were introduced to Kawau Island by former Prime Minister of New Zealand Sir George Grey around 1870, along with animals including monkeys, zebra and gnu. In 1912, dama wallabies from Kawau Island were released near Lake Okareka in the Bay of Plenty.Since then, the animals have established themselves across a large area. The Bay of Plenty Regional Council says they are now found across more than 200,000 hectares. Their current range stretches from Rotorua east to Kawerau, and south beyond Maunga Kakaramea, also known as Rainbow Mountain, towards the Paeroa Range between Reporoa and Waikite Valley.The spread is a concern because wallabies are difficult to detect. They are cautious and mainly active at night. During the day, they often shelter in dense forest or scrub. They can live in both native and exotic forests, particularly in places where forest is close to pasture or open, sunny areas.Wallabies can change forestsThe main concern is what the animals eat. Wallabies feed on native tree seedlings, ferns and grasses. If this feeding continues over a long period, it can prevent some native plants from growing and replacing older trees.This can gradually change the structure and composition of native forests. Some plants eaten selectively by wallabies are also important food sources for native birds and other wildlife.Wallabies can also cause problems outside native forests. In exotic plantations, they can damage young pine and eucalyptus seedlings. On farms, they compete with livestock for pasture, reducing the amount of food available to farm animals.The animals prefer areas where they can move between forest cover and open land. They often gather in small family groups. Their spread has been slowed in some places by natural barriers such as lakes and rivers. However, authorities say people have sometimes helped wallabies move beyond these barriers.Wallabies can spread quicklyWallabies are highly mobile and estimates their populations can spread by up to 2 kilometres a year on average. If their spread is not controlled, scientists estimate, they could eventually occupy one-third of New Zealand by 2065. Government estimates that the damage caused by wallabies could reach $84 million a year if they are left unchecked. It also says the cost of the damage is expected to increase each year.Wallabies have therefore been classified as an unwanted organism under New Zealandâs Biosecurity Act 1993. According to the law, Wallabies cannot be bred, sold, moved or exhibited without a permit.Effort to controlThe Bay of Plenty Regional Council has different management categories for wallaby species. Dama and parma wallabies are covered by eradication and progressive containment programmes.Under the eradication programme, pests are present but limited enough in their size or distribution for removal to be considered possible and cost-effective. Progressive containment is used where the aim is to stop the pest from spreading, reduce its distribution or remove it from parts of the region over time.Three other wallaby species Bennettâs wallaby, brush-tailed rock wallaby and swamp wallaby are not currently known to be established in the Bay of Plenty. These species are listed under an exclusion programme, which means the Regional Council is responsible for managing new incursions into the region.Night shooting and poisoning One method used on private farmland is night shooting. Wallabies are mostly active at night, making this approach suitable for controlling them in areas where it can be carried out safely.The Bay of Plenty Regional Council says night shooting should only be attempted by licensed and experienced shooters. It also says accurate bullet placement is essential for humane kills.Poisoning is another control option, although only limited pesticides are registered for use against wallabies. The council lists 1080 and Feratox encapsulated cyanide as the two registered pesticides.Their use is regulated, and handlers must hold a Controlled Substances Licence. The use of these pesticides is also subject to requirements from WorkSafe and the Medical Officer of Health.Wallabies can be vulnerable to aerial or hand-broadcast bait, but they do not always use bait stations. The report notes that where wallabies live alongside possums, the smaller but more aggressive possums can prevent wallabies from reaching some bait stations.People are asked to report wallabies whether they are alive or dead. Their tracks and droppings can also provide evidence of their presence.A wallaby footprint has a distinctive shape. The long hind feet can leave tracks in sand or soft soil, with a large central toe extending beyond the outer toe. Their droppings are also distinctive and are slightly larger than individual deer pellets, often with a tear-drop shape.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Bangladesh-India reset stalls over Hasina: What would break the deadlock?
articles.summary: Analysts say an Indian commitment not to allow ousted Bangladesh PM to engage in politics from their soil would help.
articles.body:
Dhaka, Bangladesh — New Delhi and Dhaka had been quietly planning Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s first visit to India since taking office earlier this year, when a news conference shattered those efforts.

Former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina, convicted of crimes against humanity in her country, addressed a news conference held in the heart of the Indian capital by video on August 5, where she, her son and their Awami League party colleagues criticised the mass uprising that had brought her down.

Bangladesh responded swiftly, saying it was “outraged” that Hasina had been allowed to speak publicly from Indian soil, where she has been in exile since her ouster in August 2024. Dhaka had specifically warned New Delhi against allowing political activities that could affect bilateral relations.

Bangladesh subsequently said a “propitious environment” was needed before the trip, while asking New Delhi to act on extradition requests involving Hasina and other fugitives.

India says the requests remain “under examination” through established procedures.

But interviews with Bangladeshi officials and analysts suggest the immediate dispute may be more nuanced than a simple extradition standoff.

The key question may be less when India hands Hasina over than what India allows her to do while she remains there.

Faisal Mahmud, a former press minister at the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi, said extradition and Hasina’s political activities should be treated as separate issues.

“The stalemate between Bangladesh and India stems largely from New Delhi giving Sheikh Hasina a literal megaphone while she remains in exile there – something Dhaka had specifically asked India not to allow,” Mahmud told Al Jazeera.

Extradition, he said, was “an entirely different matter, and a far more complicated and lengthy one” that the Rahman government understood.

“At this point, the impasse over Tarique’s proposed visit to India, and over any broader reset of the frosty bilateral relationship, is not centred on Hasina’s extradition,” Mahmud said. “It is centred on India allowing her to conduct political activities from its soil.”

That concern predates the government under Rahman’s Bangladesh Nationalist Party.

During an April 4, 2025 meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus, then head of Bangladesh’s interim administration, asked New Delhi to prevent Hasina from making what he described as “incendiary statements” from Indian soil.

Humaiun Kobir, deputy head of Bangladesh’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, told Al Jazeera that Dhaka wanted “a good and working relationship with India based on trust and mutual respect”.

“But letting terrorists like Sheikh Hasina destabilise our country from India is not acceptable,” Kobir said, using the government’s description of the former prime minister.

He argued that relations could enter “a new phase” if the leadership of both countries wanted it, but said New Delhi must recognise Bangladesh’s changed political reality following the 2024 uprising.

“No one can conduct any terror activity from a sovereign land,” Kobir said. “It is unacceptable that the terrorists who killed our people are allowed to talk from their land and incite violence in Bangladesh.”

He said Dhaka wanted India to return other Bangladeshis accused of crimes, including suspects in the killing of Sharif Osman Hadi, an outspoken critic of Hasina and India who was murdered in 2025. His alleged killers were subsequently arrested by India, where they had crossed over.

Yet Kobir’s comments also suggest Dhaka does not want the Hasina dispute to indefinitely prevent high-level engagement.

Talks over Rahman’s visit remain under way, he said, describing a meeting between the Bangladeshi and Indian prime ministers as ultimately unavoidable. Over the weekend, in fact, India’s Rashtrapati Bhavan — the presidential palace — issued a notice suggesting that it was preparing to host Rahman, only to withdraw the document hours later.

“A meeting is a must,” Kobir told Al Jazeera. “But only when it aligns with our national interest.”

“It can be next week, two weeks later or two months later,” he added.

That distinction matters because restricting Hasina’s political activity and extraditing her present very different challenges for New Delhi.

Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal after being convicted of crimes against humanity over the deadly crackdown on the 2024 uprising. She rejects the proceedings as politically motivated.

Bangladesh first formally sought Hasina’s extradition on December 23, 2024, through a diplomatic note sent under the countries’ 2013 extradition treaty.

After her death sentence in November 2025, Dhaka reiterated the request, and India subsequently said it was “under examination”.

On August 11, India’s Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said Bangladesh’s request for Sheikh Hasina’s extradition was being examined under India’s “established procedures”, adding that New Delhi would share an update when there was further progress.

The MEA did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for further details on the matter.

Pinak Ranjan Chakravarty, a former Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh, said the matter must proceed through treaty provisions and India’s legal system.

“All legal formalities have to be completed for obtaining a judicial order for extradition,” Chakravarty told Al Jazeera.

He said the treaty also contained grounds under which extradition could be refused.

Some analysts see a political contradiction in the extradition demand.

David Bergman, a veteran observer of Bangladesh politics, argues that Dhaka is pressing India to return Hasina while potentially preferring that she remain outside the country.

“Bangladesh demands extradition knowing that the Indian government will never extradite Hasina,” Bergman told Al Jazeera, adding: “It is apparently playing to the gallery of Bangladesh public opinion.”

“At the same time, the government does not actually want Hasina to return,” Bergman said, referring to a dilemma that other analysts too have pointed to: Hasina’s return could create as many political and legal problems for Dhaka as it resolves.

Bangladesh would have custody of a former prime minister sentenced to death, forcing the government to confront the politically and internationally sensitive consequences of imprisoning, and potentially executing, one of the country’s most consequential political figures.

But the Hasina question is only one part of a broader recalibration of Dhaka’s relationship with New Delhi.

Shahab Enam Khan, professor of international relations at Jahangirnagar University, said Dhaka’s current posture should not be read simply as anti-India. Khan told Al Jazeera that Bangladesh still needs trade, defence, security and people-to-people ties with India.

He said the government’s stance reflects two pressures: asserting Bangladesh’s legal and sovereign authority, and responding to public sentiment shaped by what he described as New Delhi’s close alignment with Hasina’s Awami League over the past two decades.

Khan argued that India had invested heavily in the Awami League as its principal political partner in Bangladesh and had been slow to fully adjust to the country’s post-2024 political reality.

He said New Delhi was now “increasingly embracing the political reality in Bangladesh”, but added that Dhaka needed to see that shift translated into concrete outcomes.

The political dispute has not halted practical engagement.

A Confederation of Indian Industry delegation visited Dhaka this month for talks with ministers and business leaders even as uncertainty over Rahman’s proposed India visit intensified. Bilateral merchandise trade remains above $12bn annually, with India exporting $10.56bn worth of goods to Bangladesh, according to the Indian High Commission in Dhaka.

For former Indian High Commissioner Chakravarty, that reflects an unavoidable structural reality.

“Geography is an immutable factor in geopolitics,” he told Al Jazeera. “It binds India and Bangladesh in a manner that cannot be ignored by policymakers in both countries.”

But he criticised Dhaka for attaching conditions to Rahman’s visit.

“I do not think that the larger national interest and bilateral ties should be held hostage to any individual,” Chakravarty said.

Sreeradha Datta, a professor specialising in South Asian studies at India’s OP Jindal Global University, pointed to another dimension of that interdependence: Bangladesh’s attempts to diversify its external relationships have not reduced India’s strategic importance.

She said Dhaka’s expanding engagement with the United States and China, growing defence cooperation with Turkiye and renewed outreach to Pakistan have added to New Delhi’s concerns about Bangladesh’s foreign policy direction.

China has become particularly important, Datta said, with Beijing’s sustained economic and strategic engagement giving it a growing role in Bangladesh’s development and foreign policy calculations.

Even so, she argued, Bangladesh’s broader external partnerships cannot diminish India’s structural importance.

“Neither side can stay disengaged for long,” Datta told Al Jazeera, noting that geography ensures India will remain strategically important to Bangladesh.

The two countries share a 4,096km (2,546-mile) land border.

Datta said Bangladesh also occupies a critical place in India’s eastern connectivity, security and neighbourhood strategy, adding that the relationship is supported by more than 70 bilateral mechanisms.

That structural dependence also helps explain why, despite the political standoff, New Delhi has stopped short of closing the door on high-level engagement.

As recently as August 18, the MEA said Rahman’s invitation remained open, while reiterating that New Delhi wants a “positive, constructive and forward-looking” relationship with Bangladesh based on mutual interest and reciprocity.

The unresolved question is what concession, public or private, could create enough political space for both governments to move towards a meeting without appearing to have backed down.
